title: Re-scalable Aperture for Precision Targeting Radar
label: RAPTR
role: Deputy hardware leadership / CEM & RF management
narrative: After my initial CEM toolkit and SEWIP assignments, RAPTR became my next major radar program in Baltimore. It was developed as a scalable, product-line radar offering targeting the U.S. Army's Future Vertical Lift (FVL) opportunity, alongside drone radar applications. My responsibilities included deputy hardware leadership and RF/CEM engineering management. The product approach sought adaptability across different platform and mission needs; these were target applications, not claims of selection for specific platforms. A separate, publicly documented RAPTR flight demonstration for FVL followed in December 2022, after my Baltimore tenure, and is included solely as program context. The work was associated with internal Northrop Grumman New Technology/IP recognition; specific award attribution and dates remain to be established.

title: Internal CEM Toolkit & RF Modeling
label: CEM / RF R&D
role: Algorithm development / computational electromagnetics → hardware engineering management
narrative: One of my first assignments at Northrop Grumman in Baltimore was developing a new computational method for an internal computational electromagnetics (CEM) toolkit, with the goals of handling larger electromagnetic problems and improving execution speed. I confirmed that this work produced a previously reported 100–250% performance improvement, and that the method was subsequently adopted or incorporated into the toolkit; the precise adoption route and benchmark basis have not yet been documented. Separately, I performed CEM analysis supporting SEWIP. Later responsibilities expanded to RF modeling, simulation R&D and engineering management.
